title: Copilot Notebooks: where does the content live, and who can switch it off?
summary: The creation policy, admin path, preview Graph operation, storage distinctions and quoted licensing requirements are supported. Minor corrections should acknowledge conflicting Microsoft guidance on Conditional Access and container labels, and align the monitoring checklist with the controls table.

claims.claim: Copilot Notebooks is a persistent AI workspace.
claims.quote: organize related chats, output creations, and references into a persistent AI workspace.

claims.claim: Users keep related chats, references and generated content together in a notebook.
claims.quote: Add related chats, references, and generated content to the Notebook.

claims.claim: Copilot grounds responses on the notebook's accumulated context.
claims.quote: Copilot uses the Notebook's accumulated context to ground responses, so work continues across sessions instead of starting over each time.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot app offers a quicker, lighter Notebooks experience.
claims.quote: While this is the quicker, light-weight Notebooks experience, you can still find the fuller, workspace-forward experience in OneNote.

claims.claim: The fuller Notebooks experience remains available in OneNote.
claims.quote: you can still find the fuller, workspace-forward experience in OneNote.

claims.claim: The creation setting governs Copilot Notebooks in both experiences.
claims.quote: When creation is disabled, users are unable to create new Copilot Pages or Notebooks.

claims.where: summary; What it is: Who sets what

claims.quote: Select Customization from the left pane. Select Policy Management. Create a new policy configuration or edit an existing one. From the Choose the scope dropdown list ... In Configure Settings ... Create and view Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks

claims.claim: POST /beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors can apply the setting through an applyOnce baseline using microsoft.copilot.copilotpagesnotebooks and properties.value.

claims.claim: The Cloud Policy can be scoped to all users or a selected group.
claims.quote: From the Choose the scope dropdown list, choose either All users or select the group for which you want to apply the policy.

claims.claim: The creation setting defaults to Enabled.
claims.quote: Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks creation | Cloud Policy: Create and view Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks | Enabled

claims.claim: Not configured leaves creation available.
claims.quote: Not configured: Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks creation and integration are available to the users.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits

claims.quote: When creation is disabled, users are unable to create new Copilot Pages or Notebooks.

claims.claim: A notebook can include files and Teams meeting content as references.
claims.quote: By adding meetings as knowledge sources, users can connect transcripts, notes, chats, and shared content directly to their projects, enriching notebooks beyond files alone

claims.claim: Notebook content is governed by the retention rules of its OneDrive or SharePoint Embedded storage.
claims.quote: The sections below outline governance, lifecycle, and compliance capabilities applicable to all Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks storage types.

claims.quote: Purview eDiscovery: Supported for search/collection, review (Premium license required), and export as HTML (Premium license required) or original format.

claims.claim: Notebook content remains subject to the sharing rules of its storage service rather than a separate new store.
claims.quote: Consuming tenant Microsoft 365 settings apply to app documents stored by SharePoint Embedded. This includes supported security, compliance, risk, and governance settings.

claims.claim: The admin policies page gives no individual Notebooks feature setting for reference types or audio overview beyond blocking creation.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Notebooks individual features references audio overview admin policy creation; "Copilot Notebooks" "audio" "admin" "policy". Read cpcn-admin-configuration in full; creation and Pages/Chat code-preview settings are listed, not notebook reference-type or audio controls.

claims.claim: The requirements table lists Microsoft Copilot license for Copilot Notebooks.
claims.quote: Copilot Notebooks license | Microsoft Copilot license

claims.where: Cost and licensing; What to check; Open questions
claims.claim: The requirements prose says users need the Microsoft Copilot or Copilot Chat license.
claims.quote: Users need the Microsoft Copilot or Copilot Chat license.

claims.claim: The Tenant Configuration Management page says Notebooks require a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
claims.quote: Copilot Notebooks also require a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

claims.claim: OneDrive-stored content counts against the user's OneDrive storage limit.
claims.quote: Quota | Counts against user's OneDrive storage limit

claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Notebooks" "price" "meter". Read cpcn-requirements and cpcn-storage in full; license requirements and storage quotas are stated, but no separate Notebooks price or meter. Search returned general Copilot and developer billing pages.

claims.claim: Users whose organization disabled OneDrive creation cannot create Notebooks regardless of the creation setting.
claims.quote: If your organization disabled the creation of OneDrive, regardless of the setting noted here, these people in your organization can't create Copilot Pages or Copilot Notebooks.

claims.claim: Disabling creation hides the Notebooks module in the Microsoft Copilot app.
claims.quote: the Notebooks module is hidden, preventing users from accessing existing Notebooks through the Copilot App.

claims.claim: Sharing links to Notebooks stop working when creation is disabled.
claims.quote: Sharing links to Copilot Notebooks don't work when creation is disabled via the policy in this article.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Disabling creation; Governance controls
claims.claim: The setting does not delete existing Notebooks.
claims.quote: Existing Copilot Pages and Notebooks aren't deleted.

claims.where: Risks and limits: One container, two policies
claims.claim: Either the Copilot creation policy or the Loop Create Loop workspaces in Loop policy can allow the legacy shared container to be created.
claims.quote: This single user-owned container is created when a user first needs one of these experiences and at least one of the relevant creation policies allows it.

claims.where: Risks and limits: One container, two policies
claims.claim: Both creation policies must be disabled for the same user to prevent the shared container being created.
claims.quote: To prevent the container from being created, disable both policies for the same user.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Recovery differs by storage
claims.claim: Legacy Notebooks have no end-user recycle bin.
claims.quote: There is no end-user recycle bin for Copilot Notebooks.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Recovery differs by storage
claims.claim: Administrators cannot recover individually deleted legacy Notebooks.
claims.quote: Neither administrators nor end users can recover individually deleted Copilot Notebooks.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Recovery differs by storage
claims.claim: End users cannot recover individually deleted legacy Notebooks.
claims.quote: Neither administrators nor end users can recover individually deleted Copilot Notebooks.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Recovery differs by storage
claims.claim: Deleted OneDrive-stored pages and notebooks can be found in the OneDrive recycle bin.
claims.quote: Deleted pages and notebooks can be found in the OneDrive recycle bin.

claims.claim: The Copilot compliance summary says Information Barriers are unsupported for Notebooks.
claims.quote: Information Barriers | Not supported

claims.claim: The SharePoint Embedded security page documents a beta informationBarrier property.
claims.quote: The beta Microsoft Graph fileStorageContainer resource has an informationBarrier property that lets you manage a container's information barrier.

claims.claim: The conflicting feature-specific and platform guidance leaves Information Barriers applicability to Notebooks unresolved.
claims.quote: Information Barriers are not supported for content stored in SharePoint Embedded containers. Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks use SharePoint Embedded for storage.

claims.claim: Conditional Access applies only to the entire Microsoft Copilot app.
claims.quote: Only applies at the app level. Because Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks are features of the Microsoft Copilot app, Conditional Access applies to the entire app at m365.cloud.microsoft.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with: 'The Copilot compliance summary describes Conditional Access as app-level only; the SharePoint Embedded security page separately documents container-level ConditionalAccessPolicy, so the guidance differs for legacy storage.' Both cited pages were read.

claims.claim: Notebooks have no container sensitivity label.
claims.quote: Copilot Notebooks don't have container sensitivity labels because they share a container with all Copilot Pages.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with: 'The Copilot compliance summary says Notebooks have no container sensitivity labels because they share a container with Copilot Pages; the SharePoint Embedded security page separately documents setting container sensitivity labels, so the guidance differs for legacy storage.'

claims.claim: The compliance summary attributes the lack of Notebook container labels to sharing a container with Copilot Pages.
claims.quote: because they share a container with all Copilot Pages.

claims.where: Risks and limits: No per-container quota
claims.claim: Microsoft states that administrators cannot set quota limits on individual containers.
claims.quote: There's no admin control to set quota limits on individual containers.

claims.claim: A policy change can take up to 90 minutes when policy configurations already existed.
claims.quote: If there were existing policy configurations before the change, the change takes up to 90 minutes to be reflected.

claims.claim: A policy change can take up to 24 hours when no policy configurations previously existed.
claims.quote: If there were no policy configurations before the change, the change takes up to 24 hours to be reflected.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Blocked WebSockets; What to check
claims.claim: Real-time collaboration needs WebSocket traffic to *.svc.ms and *.office.com.
claims.quote: Allow WebSocket traffic to *.svc.ms and *.office.com endpoints. WebSocket connections enable real-time collaboration features including live editing, presence indicators, and shared cursors.

claims.claim: Office Apps Administrator is the recommended Cloud Policy role.
claims.quote: Office Apps Administrator (Recommended)

claims.claim: Security Administrator is also supported for managing Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: You can use the following built-in Microsoft Entra roles for accessing and managing the feature: ... Security Administrator

claims.claim: Global Administrator is also supported for managing Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: Global Administrator | This role can manage all aspects of Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft services that use Microsoft Entra identities.

claims.claim: AI Administrator is the least-privileged signed-in user role for Graph remediation and applyOnce.
claims.quote: AI Administrator is the least-privileged role for the signed-in user for remediation and applyOnce; don't assign that user-role requirement to the service principal.

claims.claim: Subset enablement assigns Enabled to Group A and Disabled to All users, with Group A at the lower priority number.
claims.quote: In Cloud Policy, lower priority numbers are evaluated first. With this configuration, users in Group A get the policy Enabled, while all other users in Group B get it Disabled.

claims.claim: The Graph Tenant Configuration Management route is preview and uses Microsoft Graph beta.
claims.quote: This article lists the Copilot resource types supported in preview for monitoring and snapshots through the Tenant Configuration Management (TCM) APIs in Microsoft Graph beta.

claims.claim: The baseline resourceType for the setting is microsoft.copilot.copilotpagesnotebooks.
claims.quote: "resourceType": "microsoft.copilot.copilotpagesnotebooks"

claims.claim: The resource uses properties.value as a string, with 0 disabling and 1 enabling the setting.
claims.quote: value | Write | String | Allows or prevents creating and viewing Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks through Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Copilot Actions. 0 disables the setting; 1 enables the setting.

claims.claim: The configuration monitor mode defaults to monitorOnly.
claims.quote: mode | monitorMode | The monitor mode. The possible values are: monitorOnly, applyOnce, unknownFutureValue. Optional; defaults to monitorOnly.

claims.claim: applyOnce applies the desired-state baseline once.
claims.quote: or applies a desired-state baseline once in applyOnce mode.

claims.claim: monitorOnly detects configuration drift rather than applying the baseline.
claims.quote: to detect configuration drift in monitorOnly mode, or applies a desired-state baseline once in applyOnce mode.

claims.claim: TCM supports the setting only in tenant-level policies.
claims.quote: TCM supports these settings only in tenant-level policies in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.

claims.claim: A group-level policy for the same setting makes monitoring and remediation fail.
claims.quote: Before using TCM, ensure that the target setting isn't configured in any group-level policy in that admin center. If it is, monitoring, snapshots, remediation, and applyOnce fail for that resource.

claims.claim: Audit logs are available for all events.
claims.quote: Audit logs: Available for all events. Retained, exportable, and streamable to third-party tools.

claims.claim: The audit logs can be searched in Purview.
claims.quote: Search in Purview for "page" and filter by "SourceFileExtension":"page".

claims.claim: eDiscovery review of Notebooks needs a Premium license.
claims.quote: review (Premium license required)

claims.claim: eDiscovery HTML export of Notebooks needs a Premium license.
claims.quote: export as HTML (Premium license required) or original format.

claims.claim: Retention policies configured for all SharePoint sites are enforced for Notebooks.
claims.quote: Retention policies from Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management configured for all SharePoint sites are enforced for all Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks.

claims.claim: The creation setting does not set sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: Admin policy: Use Cloud Policy to turn on or off creation of Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks. ... Sensitivity labels: Available for Copilot Pages.

claims.claim: The creation setting does not configure retention.
claims.quote: Retention policies from Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management configured for all SharePoint sites are enforced for all Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks.

claims.claim: The creation setting does not configure Conditional Access.
claims.quote: Conditional Access applies to the entire app at m365.cloud.microsoft. Use admin policies to block creation of new content.

claims.claim: The user-owned container can need to be manually added as an eDiscovery data source.
claims.quote: Until then, retrieve the user-owned container URL using PowerShell or the SharePoint admin center, then add it as a data source manually.

claims.where: What to check; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist names Purview audit searching and eDiscovery data-source configuration, but the controls table contains only the creation policy.
claims.quote: Search the Purview audit log for the `.pod` file extension ... Confirm that your eDiscovery managers know to add the user-owned container as a data source. Table: Whether users can create and view Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks.
claims.fix: Remove the two checklist bullets beginning 'Search the Purview audit log' and 'Confirm that your eDiscovery managers' so the checklist does not direct readers to controls absent from the table. Keep the supported Watching prose; do not add control rows in this correction.
